title: Poultry House — Yasnaya Polyana
visualBrief: Complete independent small log poultry-house interpretation: slightly irregular mapped walls, white plinth, brown recessed gable door and white-framed divided window, closed timber gables, steep weathered-gray roof with closed eave/fascia thickness, corner log ends and a supported approach stair. Use shared wood_log, wood_plain, wood_vertical, shingle_cedar, plaster_lime and storefront surfaces. The companion red-roof shed remains a separate model; no trees, copied signs, people or photo pixels are baked in.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Two adjacent retained one-story shed footprints are candidates for the small gray-gabled poultry house and longer red-hipped equipment shed shown together in the ordinary museum photograph. Sizes and separation support this assignment. The retained long axes are nearly parallel; the photograph may show different faces through perspective/parallax, and no camera position is known. Specific poultry/equipment function and absolute front assignment remain explicit photo/relative-context inferences; the public map names both only as sheds. Use the photographed gray roof on the small building despite the generic map red-roof tag. This small mapped footprint supplies8.46x5.72m scale; localX southeast is the inferred door/window gable. Its mapped neighbor remains independent. Source axes are baked east/up/south, heading0.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Photo-led wall2.45m, gray pitched ridge4.8m above floor; brown door.98x2.12m at left and white-framed.88x1.13m window at right. Floor 0.9195721926610361m above outside datum and.15m above the highest retained corner. Coarse ground varies.88m across the footprint; exposed white plinth is.15..1.03m and is larger than parts of the photo. 5supported approach treads reconcile the native grade. Roof finish/pitch, course/bay counts, hidden rear and historic thresholds remain approximations.
